references.text: God brought them out of Egypt; he has strength like a wild ox. The same image of God's power compared to a wild ox (re'em) is used regarding Israel.
God brought him out of Egypt; he has strength like a wild ox. He shall devour hostile nations and break their bones. A parallel reference to the wild ox's horns goring against the peoples.
Jacob's blessing over Ephraim and Manasseh, where Ephraim is placed before Manasseh. Explains why Ephraim is mentioned with tens of thousands and Manasseh with thousands.
Jacob's blessing over Joseph, who is the father of Ephraim and Manasseh. Contains promises of fruitfulness and strength.
You have lifted my horn like that of a wild ox. The same image of the wild ox's horns as a symbol of strength and exaltation.
Deliver me from the lion's mouth, from the horns of the wild ox. The wild ox's horns as an image of mighty power.
The tribe of Manasseh numbered 32,200 men, while the tribe of Ephraim numbered 40,500. Confirms that Ephraim was larger than Manasseh in number.
Joshua speaks to the house of Joseph, Ephraim and Manasseh, about their great numbers and strength. Describes the significant size of the tribes.
